- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect market resilience.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to forecast peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price peaks in late period (last 7–10 days); apply +1–2% upward adjustment to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in adjusting; anticipate 1–2 days of delay and adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead.
